subject: What's on in E2 · 15–21 October: a free Sebright bill and Somali Week
preheader: A free three-band bill at the Sebright, Somali Week at Oxford House, a late Saturday at the Working Men's Club and Halloween dates.

items.blurb: A three-band bill of dream punk, post punk and grunge in the Sebright's basement gig room, below the ground-floor bar. Entry is free, so it's an easy yes.

sections.heading: Nights worth crossing the road for
sections.lede: Two very different Saturday nights: one in the heart of E2, one a short walk away.

items.headline: Margo Marshall at the Working Men's Club
items.blurb: A late club night at Bethnal Green Working Men's Club with Margo Marshall billed. Advance tickets start at £8, and it runs until 2am, so pace yourself.

items.headline: Chudahye Chagis at Rich Mix
items.blurb: A K-Music Festival gig whose genre is listed as psychedelic shamanic funk, so one for the curious. Rich Mix is a charity-run arts centre, which makes a change from a pub back room.

items.headline: DJ Crooks & Goons at the Star
items.blurb: A Friday DJ night at the Star of Bethnal Green, a local pub with a disco-and-karaoke reputation. It runs until 2am.

items.headline: A history workshop on Saturday afternoon
items.blurb: A Saturday-afternoon workshop with Dr Peggy Brunache at the local history library, a change of pace from a night out. The price isn't listed, so check before you go.

items.headline: TRMNL London at 93 Feet East
items.blurb: House and tech house at 93 Feet East on Brick Lane, from 3pm to midnight. An early start for people who like to dance and still get home at a sensible hour.

sections.heading: Comedy, a festival and a closing show
sections.lede: A festival, a comedy bill and the last days of a gallery show, all close to the tube.

items.headline: Somali Week at Oxford House
items.blurb: Somali Week at Oxford House, the Bethnal Green community arts centre, with events running to 25 October. The festival is listed as free, though individual events may carry their own ticket prices.

items.headline: Comedy, a film and music at Oxford House
items.blurb: An evening of comedy from Naif Mohammed, Khalid Raheem, Prince Abdi and Selam Amare, followed by a film screening and music. It runs from 6pm to 10pm, and the price isn't listed.

items.headline: Last days of LAG at Soft Opening
items.blurb: Maren Karlson's show at Soft Opening, a gallery on Minerva Street, closes on 17 October. This is the last chance to see it.

items.headline: A Monday bill at the Sebright
items.blurb: A multi-act bill at the Sebright on a Monday for £6, a cheap early-in-the-week reason to go out.

items.headline: Sunday records at Mare Street Market
items.blurb: A Sunday-lunchtime DJ session at Mare Street Market, a Hackney market of independent restaurants and shops. Entry is free.

items.headline: Open mic at Oxford House
items.blurb: An open mic evening for Black History Month at Oxford House. Entry is listed as free, with donations welcome.

items.headline: Free vinyl sessions on Curtain Road
items.blurb: Vinyl-only DJ sets with a downtempo slant at 26 Curtain Road in Shoreditch, with entry listed as free. Worth the trip if you like your music played from records.

items.headline: Bubbledee at Colour Factory
items.blurb: A house music night at Colour Factory, a club and live music space in Queen's Yard, Hackney Wick. Tickets are from £15, it starts at 10pm and it's over-18s only.

sections.heading: Regular nights
sections.lede: Ones that come round again, if you miss them this week.

sections.heading: Book now
sections.lede: Halloween lands on a Saturday this year, and the parties start the night before.

notes_for_fred: Pick is the free Sebright bill on Thursday 15 Oct, the day the email goes out. The alternative is BRAT 2 SCHOOL at the Working Men's Club (Sat, 9pm-2am), but its record names only one act, so I kept it as a featured card.

Prices are missing on several events used: LAG, the history workshop, the Oxford House comedy night, TRMNL, Jubel, Cheese & Wine. The blurbs say so only where it matters; compact lines show nothing about cost.
Somali Week is listed as free, but the festival page also says individual events carry their own ticket prices. The blurb says that. Worth a glance.

Food and community are thin for this exact week (one tasting, one workshop), so there are no sections for them: the tasting sits in Regular nights, the workshop in More worth a look, and Book now carries Day of the Dead and the Cheese & Wine night.
SEND Play at Young V&A is in the data as an ongoing run but is on the first Saturday of the month, so nothing falls in this week. Left out.
20 events, near the top of the range. 'Regular nights' carries a £30 cider tasting beside free events; swap it out if it feels odd there.
The Oxford House comedy night's ticket link is the Somali Week festival page, not a page for that night. Probably fine as the festival hub, but worth a click before it goes out.
